policy.description: Blocking line-coverage ratchets. For a fixed scope, coveredLines is the highest value in the reviewed clean-run observation envelope, never a modal or repeated lower value, and that high-water never decreases. Update the envelope in the same reviewed change whenever scope or coverage advances. A fixed-scope floor may move downward only to the exact minimum directly observed by clean runs on the identical source, tests, and total-line scope, with linked evidence and a bounded tolerance; unexplained coverage loss remains a regression.

tolerance.rationale: Issue #717 adds a lazy identity- and navigation-fenced awards details module and its focused tests outside the fixed Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinCanopy/src/core/** instrumentation scope, rebased on the combined #718/#732/#733 main tree. Two clean full client runs on this exact 273-file and 2,629-test tree passed every test and both measured 2,976/3,362 core lines (88.519%) without instrumentation spread. The reviewed observed high-water and exact observed floor therefore remain 2,976/3,362 with zero tolerance; the prior #718 evidence established this core source scope, while these runs establish the same exact ratchet against the expanded issue #717 tree. coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact below-floor, above-baseline, scope-change, observed-high-water, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.

Canonical Series relationship-string reuse changes the complete assembly scope from 57,155 to 57,163 instrumented lines. The accompanying paused-handoff regression owns its dedicated producer thread and observes queue admission separately from thread startup, preserving the original one-second admission deadline and losslessness checks. Two clean full runs on the identical 601-file production/test/build-input scope at Canopy commit aa6105355e6d13dfbb3ff9fba8bc981c6182b255, using SDK 10.0.302/runtime 10.0.10, each passed all 4,716 tests and measured 47,256/57,163 and 47,254/57,163. Both raw Cobertura reports and full logs are retained, with identical class/file/line keys and verified source hashes after the main update. These observations establish high-water 47,256, directly observed floor 47,254, and exactly two lines of tolerance (about 0.0035 percentage points). TagCacheDependencyGraph coverage advances from 242/270 to 258/277 and TagCacheService from 1,847/1,938 to 1,849/1,939; both changed owners have identical coverage in the two new runs. Six differing Boolean line hits in existing PlatformProviderInvocationService and PlatformProviderRegistryOrchestrator lifecycle branches produce the two-line net spread. No changed-owner coverage is lost, and no failing-test or different-source measurement is included. The policy, client baseline, coverage implementation, original worker-allocation budgets and queue-admission deadline remain unchanged. coverage-baseline.test.js rejects 47,253, requires review above 47,256, and rejects either neighboring total-line scope or an unevidenced broader envelope.
